patch_description: Replace the exponentially-weighted moving average (which introduces systematic lag and fails to smooth reversals well) with a two-stage approach: (1) a constant-velocity Kalman filter that adaptively estimates local signal level and slope with measurement-noise estimation, and (2) a short Savitzky-Golay-style polynomial smoother applied on top to further suppress slope changes and false reversals. The Kalman filter's predictive step compensates for the group delay of the smoothing, dramatically reducing lag error while the process-noise adaptation preserves genuine trend dynamics (tracking accuracy). Output is re-indexed to match the existing sliding-window length convention so downstream code is unchanged. This addresses all four objectives: fewer spurious slope changes, low lag, good trend tracking, and fewer false reversals, while remaining O(N) and fast.
